title: Re-baseline val_half against the official ByteTrack YOLOX: the headline RF-DETR win may not survive
description:
mot-n2n.3 established that the 'yoloxx20' baseline used in every val_half comparison is NOT ByteTrack's released MOT20 detector. It came from a supplied bundle and is measurably weaker than the official checkpoint on the same val_half frames:

  metric        supplied yoloxx20   yoloxx20-official
  mAP@50               0.9000              0.9683
  mAP@75               0.8278              0.8798
  mAP@50:95            0.6759              0.7135
  AR@50:95             0.7104              0.7553

THE RISK. This project's headline result is that RF-DETR beats the ByteTrack baseline on tracking despite losing on detection: arm D 70.883 HOTA vs yoloxx20 70.208 (docs/results-reference.md section 7.1), a margin of 0.675. That margin was measured against the weaker model. The official detector is +0.038 mAP@50:95 and +0.045 AR, and on full MOT20 train it already reaches 76.311 HOTA against I4's 75.968. If the same ordering holds on val_half, THE HEADLINE CLAIM INVERTS.

WHAT TO DO. Detections already exist: artifacts/tracking/detections/yoloxx20-official/val_half (685,373 rows, registered, checksummed). Remaining work is embeddings for both ReID models, two BoostTrack runs, two TrackEval runs. Roughly 1-1.5 h wall clock on free GPUs; no training. Follow the exact protocol of the existing yoloxx20 rows so the comparison is like-for-like: btpp-default, det_thresh 0.40, no overrides.

THEN. Whatever the result, docs/results-reference.md, docs/experiment-report.md and docs/tracker-improvements.md all frame their conclusions against the old baseline and will need revising. Keep BOTH baselines in the tables, clearly distinguished - the supplied bundle is still a legitimately measured detector, it is just not the ByteTrack release, and pooling them would be wrong.

CAVEAT THAT DOES NOT GO AWAY. Neither YOLOX is held out on val_half; both were trained on the full MOT20 train set. This re-baseline makes the comparison honest about WHICH detector, not about contamination.

Weights: weights/bytetrack_x_mot20.tar sha256 021d7bc47fe20ae690007454cd2192df6237c2f4446ae92737a79523de89de64.
Inference: tracking/scripts/infer_yoloxx20.py.
Discovered from mot-n2n.3, 2026-09-09.
close_reason:
Complete 2026-09-09. THE HEADLINE CLAIM INVERTS. The official ByteTrack YOLOX-X
beats every RF-DETR configuration on val_half.

MOT20 val_half, BoostTrack++ defaults, det_thresh 0.40, identical protocol on
every row:

  run                              HOTA     DetA     AssA     LocA     MOTA     IDF1
  yoloxx20-official / osnet      76.543   79.495   73.768   87.627   92.396   88.714
  yoloxx20-official / fastreid   76.169   79.549   73.005   87.646   92.337   87.587
  rfdetr2xl-i4-e8 / osnet        75.865   78.806   73.110   87.480   91.986   88.637
  armd-e9-t015 / osnet           70.883   72.976   68.983   85.321   87.979   85.838
  yoloxx20 (supplied) / osnet    70.208   73.496   67.133   88.177   85.031   82.536

WHAT CHANGED. The project's headline result was arm D 70.883 vs baseline 70.208,
a +0.675 RF-DETR win. Measured against the actual ByteTrack release, arm D
TRAILS BY 5.660 HOTA. Even the contamination-matched I4 build trails by 0.678.
The supplied bundle understated the real baseline by 6.335 HOTA.

The gain is in both HOTA components, DetA +5.999 and AssA +6.635 over the
supplied bundle, so it is not a post-processing or threshold artifact. One
metric moves the other way: LocA 88.177 -> 87.627, so the official detector
localizes marginally worse while tracking far better. That also weakens the
framing of mot-gpf, which treats LocA as the largest remaining gap - the model
with the best LocA on this split is now the one with the WORST HOTA.

CONTAMINATION IS UNCHANGED AND SYMMETRIC. Neither YOLOX is held out on val_half;
both trained on all of MOT20 train. I4 is likewise contaminated. Arm D is the
only held-out row in the table. So the fair like-for-like pair is
I4 75.865 vs yoloxx20-official 76.543, and the baseline still wins by 0.678.
This re-baseline makes the comparison honest about WHICH DETECTOR, not about
contamination.

METHOD. Detections were already exported and checksummed under mot-n2n.3
(685,373 rows). This issue added embeddings for both ReID models, two
BoostTrack++ runs, two TrackEval runs. No training. Both ReID models verified
distinct before use (osnet dim 512 test_dataset False, fastreid dim 2048
test_dataset True) under the guard added in mot-n2n.3.

DOCUMENTS UPDATED.
 - docs/results-reference.md REGENERATED; both baselines now appear in sections
   7.1 and 7.2, the legend distinguishes them, and the scope caveats state they
   are different models that must never be pooled. Generator --check exits 0.
 - docs/experiment-report.md and docs/tracker-improvements.md carry a
   SUPERSEDED banner at the top: their measurements stand, their interpretation
   relative to the baseline does not.
 - docs/mot20-train-evaluation.md section 1 carries the val_half tracking table.

FOLLOW-UP THIS CREATES. The retrain issues mot-ayx, mot-gpf and mot-x82 are all
justified by "closing the gap to the baseline". The gap is now 5.66 HOTA rather
than a win, and its composition changed, so their motivation should be re-read
before any GPU time is spent. mot-gpf in particular targets LocA, which is no
longer the discriminating metric.

Nothing committed; no commit was authorized.

title: Establish that the yoloxx20 baseline is not held out on val_half
description:
val_half is the second temporal half of the MOT20 *train* sequences. Determine
whether the published baseline detector trained on those frames.

Evidence: `docs/experiment-report.md` section 0, `datasets/README.md`.
close_reason:
Done, and the answer is yes. This is a material correction to every
cross-detector number in the project.

`bytetrack_x_mot20.tar` is ByteTrack's MOT20 *test* model, trained on
`mix_mot20_ch` = the full MOT20 train set plus CrowdHuman. val_half is the
second half of that train set, so the baseline has seen every frame it is
scored on. The RF-DETR arms have not.

Verified three ways. (1) val_half images are byte-identical to the original
train frames: md5 of frame 1 and the last frame of each sequence matches
MOT20-01[216,429], -02[1393,2782], -03[1204,2405], -05[1659,3315]. (2) The
`yoloxx20` variant manifest reads exactly
`datasets/val_half/{sequence}/det_yoloxx20/det_yoloxx20.txt` for 580,369
detections, which equals those four files' row count. (3) `datasets/README.md`
already labelled them "YOLOX-X detections from the MOT20-trained detector" and
warned they "should not be treated as clean detector holdout measurements".

Corroborating: BoostTrack's own `default_settings.py` selects
`bytetrack_x_mot20.tar` only when `args.test_dataset` is set, otherwise falling
back with the comment "Just use the mot17 test model as the ablation model for
20". And ByteTrack publishes no MOT20 half-split ablation model at all.

Consequence: every RF-DETR-vs-YOLOX delta is a LOWER BOUND. Arm D's +0.569 HOTA
is a win over a detector that had the answers. Arm-to-arm deltas are unaffected.

Root cause of the documentation failure: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` recorded
Stage 1 as "held out for both detector and ReID", true of the RF-DETR side
only, and every downstream document inherited it. Corrected in three files.

title: det_thresh sweep on val_half for RF-DETR: 0.4 is a YOLOX-tuned default
description:
Question: BoostTrack's MOT20 det_thresh of 0.4 was tuned for YOLOX score distributions. RF-DETR is DETR-based with no NMS and a different score distribution; Roboflow's own examples use 0.5. Is 0.4 leaving HOTA on the table?

Prior evidence: on rfdetr2xl-e5-t005, det_thresh 0.4/0.5/0.6 gave HOTA 68.08/68.35/68.02, so 0.5 already beat 0.4 by +0.27. That sweep was never repeated on the best variant.

Baseline: det_thresh 0.4. Changed variable: det_thresh only. Success metric: HOTA, with DetA/AssA/IDSW to show the mechanism.

Detectors: rfdetr2xl-arme-e19-t010-nms070 on val_half, plus yoloxx20-official as control to separate 'better MOT20 setting' from 'RF-DETR-specific'. The dead-knob lesson from the association sweep applies: any tuning claim must be checked against the other detector before it is believed.

Note det_thresh is applied to BOOSTED scores after DLO/DUO, not to raw detector scores - see docs/tracker-parameters.md Stage 6 and cross-stage coupling 3.

Non-goals: changing the detection export floor or NMS; postprocessing (separate issue).

title: Postprocessing rungs on val_half: raw vs DTI vs DTI+GBI
description:
Question: how much of our gap to upstream BoostTrack++ figures is the postprocessing protocol we skip? Upstream scores the _post_gbi folder; we score raw.

Baseline: existing raw val_half tracks. Changed variable: postprocessing stage only (tracker untouched, detections untouched). Success metric: HOTA/MOTA/IDF1/IDSW/Frag deltas per rung.

Three rungs scored separately so the two stages are not conflated: raw, +DTI (linear gap fill), +DTI+GBI (gradient-boosting smoothing on top).

Detectors: rfdetr2xl-arme-e19-t010-nms070 (derived to val_half, see mot-n2n.5 child) and yoloxx20-official. Both trained on the full MOT20 train split, so BOTH are training-set fit on val_half - a matched contaminated pair, and must be labelled as such. No row may be pooled with a held-out val_half figure.

Measured headroom on train: 51,749 DTI-eligible gap frames for arm E (4.39% of emitted rows), 51,835 for yolox.

Non-goals: tuning DTI/GBI parameters; running on test; comparing against held-out arms.
close_reason: Postprocess rungs measured on val_half for arm E and yoloxx20-official; DTI+GBI = +0.555 HOTA for arm E, -0.079 for YOLOX. Numbers to be written into docs/tracker-improvements.md

title: Understand how BoostTrack++ actually tracks today, on train, before extending test runs
description:
Requested by the user 2026-09-09: 'I want to run BoostTrack++ on test, even before that on the train itself I want to dig deep into how tracking is being done today.'

STATE OF PLAY - THE RUNS ALREADY EXIST, THE UNDERSTANDING DOES NOT.
  train: 6 combinations under artifacts/tracking/{tracks,metrics}/*/train, from
         mot-n2n.3 (I4, arm E, yoloxx20-official x osnet, fastreid).
  test:  I4 + fastreid delivered under mot-h1d, 618,775 rows, no ground truth.
  val_half: ~35 runs including the full association sweep.
So this is NOT 'run the tracker'. It is 'explain what the tracker is doing to our detections, mechanistically, with measurements'.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. Three findings say the tracker is where the leverage is and that we do not understand it:
  1. Association hyperparameters are FLAT. ~23 configurations spread ~0.4 HOTA,
     and dlo_boost_coef 0.3 vs 0.7 produced BYTE-IDENTICAL output. Either those
     knobs are inert on our data or they are not reaching the code path.
     dlo_boost_coef producing identical files is a bug-shaped result.
  2. RF-DETR feeds the tracker 283 boxes/frame against YOLOX's 130, yet output
     is 140.5 vs 120.6. Most of that surplus is discarded somewhere and we have
     only a per-stage count (docs/results-reference.md section 6), not an
     account of WHICH boxes die and why.
  3. Detection quality and tracking quality disagree in rank (mAP says A>B,
     HOTA says B>A). Whatever mediates that disagreement lives in the tracker.

WHAT TO PRODUCE, on the train split, using the existing artifacts:
  a. A written walkthrough of the actual BoostTrack++ update path as vendored in
     repos/BoostTrack: detection confidence boosting (DLO/DUO/DUC), the ECC
     camera-motion step, the Mahalanobis and shape and IoU cost terms, how the
     ReID embedding is combined, the Hungarian assignment, and track birth,
     survival and death. Cite file and line; do not paraphrase the paper.
  b. Confirm which settings are actually live. Start with dlo_boost_coef, whose
     0.3/0.7 runs are byte-identical on val_half. Determine whether MOT20's
     dataset_specific_settings override it, whether the code path is reached at
     all, and whether the same holds on train.
  c. Per-stage box accounting extended from counts to FATES: for a sample of
     frames, classify every raw detection as promoted, matched, started a new
     track, suppressed as duplicate, or dropped below threshold, and attribute
     the RF-DETR surplus specifically.
  d. Where the ID switches come from. 1,845-2,480 IDSW on train against 2,215
     real identities. Bucket them: occlusion, crowd density, camera motion,
     appearance ambiguity, or detector dropout.
  e. Name the two or three levers worth testing, with a prediction for each.
     If the answer is 'the tracker is near its ceiling on these detections',
     that is a valid and useful outcome and should be stated plainly.

THEN AND ONLY THEN, extend to test. Test has no public ground truth, so nothing
there can be scored; test runs are deliverables, not experiments. Any tracker
change must be justified on train or val_half first, and every test output stays
local_test_adapted per docs/MOTPolicy.md.

Read first: repos/BoostTrack/tracker/boost_track.py, tracker/embedding.py,
tracker/ecc.py, default_settings.py, tracking/scripts/run_boosttrack.py,
tracking/scripts/diagnose_stages.py, docs/results-reference.md section 6.
Mostly CPU work on stored artifacts; no training and little GPU.

title: Arm E2: continue arm E to 100 epochs on 6 GPUs, stop early if held-out proxy stops rising
description:
Requested by the user 2026-09-09. Continue the arm E contaminated-validation diagnostic well past its 20 epochs to see how far training-set fit keeps climbing and where it finally flattens.

TARGET: up to 100 epochs total. 6 GPUs. Stop before 100 if the metric stops increasing.

STARTING POINT: finetuning/artifacts/rfdetr-2xl-arme-diagnostic-2026-09-08-r1/checkpoint_19.ckpt
Verified to be a full Lightning checkpoint: epoch=19, global_step=10120, state_dict, optimizer_states, lr_schedulers, and callbacks including RFDETREMACallback (EMA weights) and BestModelCallback. A true resume is therefore possible in principle.

BLOCKER TO SETTLE FIRST - THERE IS NO RESUME PLUMBING.
finetuning/scripts/train_rfdetr_2xl.py only passes pretrain_weights=<path>, which loads WEIGHTS ONLY and starts a fresh run at epoch 0. It never restores optimizer state, EMA state, LR-scheduler position, or the epoch counter. So 'resume' has two meanings and they are not equivalent:
  (a) TRUE RESUME - add a ckpt_path passthrough to Lightning's Trainer.fit so
      optimizer, EMA, scheduler and epoch counter continue from 20. Faithful
      continuation of the same run; this is what 'resume' should mean.
  (b) WARM START - initialize from arm E's epoch-19 weights and run a fresh
      schedule. Simpler, no code change, but the LR schedule restarts and the
      EMA buffer resets, so it is a NEW run that happens to start from good
      weights, not a continuation. Its curve would not be comparable to arm E's.
RECOMMEND (a). Confirm with the user before building it.

DEVIATION THE USER CHOSE, RECORD IT: 7 GPUs -> 6.
Effective batch goes 4 x 2 x 7 = 56 to 4 x 2 x 6 = 48. Steps per epoch goes 506 -> 590 on the same 28,322 images. Consequences:
  - Arm E2 epoch N is NO LONGER step-comparable with arm E epoch N or I4 epoch N.
    The deliberate I4 parity that arm E was built to preserve is forfeited.
    Report arm E2 against OPTIMISER STEPS, not epochs.
  - Resuming a Lightning checkpoint under a changed world size is not a
    well-defined operation. Optimizer tensors restore fine, but global_step
    accounting and the LR schedule position were computed at the old batch size.
    Verify the first post-resume epoch does not show a loss discontinuity, and
    abort if it does.
  - lr is unchanged at 5e-5 while the batch shrinks ~14%, so the effective
    learning rate per sample rises slightly. Left as-is unless the user says
    otherwise.

STOP RULE: 100 epochs max, or stop once 6 consecutive epochs fail to beat the running best EMA mAP@50:95 - the same rule arm E used. Note this metric is measured on val_half, which is INSIDE the training set, so it is a training-set-fit measure. 'Stops increasing' here means the model has stopped fitting its own training data further; it says nothing about generalization.

WHAT THIS BUYS. Arm E's curve was still rising monotonically at epoch 19 (EMA 0.6025 -> 0.7588, no turnover). We do not know where training-set fit saturates. Arm E2 finds that ceiling, which bounds how much of the I4-vs-arm-E gap is 'more fitting' versus a genuine capacity limit.

WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY. It cannot say anything about held-out quality. Arm E trained on all 8,931 MOT20 train frames AND all 19,370 CrowdHuman images (15,000 train + 4,370 val), so no held-out set exists on disk for it. See docs/mot20-train-evaluation.md section 4.

COST: ~22 min/epoch at 7 GPUs, so roughly 26 min/epoch at 6. 80 more epochs is about 35 hours. Checkpoint_interval=1 at ~2.0 GB/epoch is ~160 GB for 80 epochs; disk is at 98% with ~200 GB free, so RAISE checkpoint_interval or prune as you go, or the run will fill the disk.

Config to derive from: finetuning/configs/rfdetr_2xl_i5-arm-e-contaminated-val-diagnostic.toml
Launcher to derive from: finetuning/scripts/run_rfdetr_2xl_arm_e_diagnostic.sh (nproc=7 -> 6)
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-09: the 'no resume plumbing' blocker in the description was WRONG. RF-DETR's TrainConfig already has a first-class `resume` field (config.py:1033) forwarded verbatim to Lightning's trainer.fit(ckpt_path=...) (detr.py:998). train_rfdetr_2xl.py forwards the whole [training] table via model.train(**training), so setting resume= in the TOML is sufficient. NO LAUNCHER CODE CHANGE WAS NEEDED. Option (a), true resume, is what runs.

VERIFIED checkpoint_19.ckpt carries: epoch=19, global_step=10120, 1 optimizer state, lr_schedulers with last_epoch=10120, and callback state for RFDETREMACallback + BestModelCallback.

CONFIG  finetuning/configs/rfdetr_2xl_i5-arm-e2-continue-100e-6gpu.toml
LAUNCH  finetuning/scripts/run_rfdetr_2xl_arm_e2_continue.sh
RUN DIR finetuning/artifacts/rfdetr-2xl-arme2-continue-2026-09-09-r1

LR SCHEDULE CHANGED, user decision 2026-09-09: step -> cosine, min_factor 0.05.
Arm E carried lr_drop=24 inherited from I4 (epochs=8) where it never fired. At
100 epochs it would fire for the first time, and NOT at epoch 24: the boundary
is lr_drop*steps_per_epoch = 24*590 = 14,160 global steps, which a run resuming
at step 10,120 reaches at epoch ~26.9, leaving 73 of 80 new epochs at 5e-6. A
10x cliff mid-diagnostic makes the fit curve unreadable. Cosine measured:
4.695e-5 at the resume step (6% below arm E's 5e-5, effectively continuous),
4.228e-5 @e30, 2.877e-5 @e50, 8.474e-6 @e80, 2.500e-6 final. TrainConfig
accepts the table with no warnings.

This SHARPENS the I7 fork rather than blunting it: under a monotonically
decaying LR, training-set fit should rise monotonically if the model is merely
fitting. A DECLINE cannot then be overfitting and cannot be too-high LR, which
leaves mixture interference (the 68.4% CrowdHuman share) as the live cause.

CHECKPOINTING: interval 10 (RF-DETR default), ~16 GB over 80 epochs vs ~160 GB
at arm E's interval 1. Nothing is lost: trainer.py:265 only builds the
per-epoch last.ckpt when checkpoint_interval != 1, so arm E2 gets per-epoch
crash recovery that arm E did not have; BestModelCallback is always on and
independent of the interval; metrics.csv logs every epoch at eval_interval=1
and is where the diagnostic curve actually comes from.

BEST-CHECKPOINT CAVEAT: arm E2's output_dir differs from the resumed
checkpoint's dir, and PTL's ModelCheckpoint.load_state_dict only restores
best_model_score when dirpaths match exactly. So arm E2's checkpoint_best_*.pth
is the best of epochs 20-99, not the best overall. Arm E's own peak (EMA 0.7588
@e19) is in its metrics.csv. And 'best' remains best-on-TRAINING-DATA either
way, because the split is contaminated. It selects nothing.

title: Full MOT20 train evaluation: I4, arm E, yoloxx20 - detection mAP + TrackEval
description:
User request 2026-09-09: detection mAP and full TrackEval metrics for three detectors on the ENTIRE MOT20 train split (8,931 frames, MOT20-01/02/03/05 at full length), not val_half.

Detectors:
  1. I4  - finetuning/artifacts/rfdetr-2xl-i4-competition-2026-09-08-r1/last_ema.pth (epoch 8, the deliverable)
  2. arm E - finetuning/artifacts/rfdetr-2xl-arme-diagnostic-2026-09-08-r1 epoch 19 (best == last)
  3. yoloxx20 - ByteTrack YOLOX-X MOT20, INFERRED here. No detections existed for this split.

ReID: both osnet-ain-msdc and fastreid-sbs-s50-mot20 (user choice), to match results-reference sections 7.1/7.2.

CONTAMINATION - EVERY NUMBER FROM THIS SPLIT IS TRAINING-SET FIT, NOT GENERALIZATION.
All three detectors trained on 100% of MOT20 train:
  - I4 COCO manifest holds 8,931/8,931 MOT20 train frames (verified: MOT20-01 429, -02 2782, -03 2405, -05 3315).
  - Arm E uses I4's dataset recipe, same coverage.
  - yoloxx20 is documented as trained on the complete MOT20 train set.
No row here may be placed in the same table as a val_half held-out figure. User approved proceeding with this labelled explicitly.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH MEASURING: full-length sequences run up to 3,315 frames vs val_half's 1,657, so association is stressed much harder; and all three models are contaminated to a comparable degree, so the three-way comparison retains meaning even though absolute values are inflated.

YOLOX PROVENANCE: weights/bytetrack_x_mot20.tar, sha256 021d7bc47fe20ae690007454cd2192df6237c2f4446ae92737a79523de89de64, 792,835,731 bytes, downloaded 2026-09-09 from the official ByteTrack Google Drive release (id 1HX2_JpMOjOIj1Z9rJjoet9XNy_cCAs5U) linked in repos/ByteTrack/README.md line 169. Byte count matches the independent HuggingFace mirror backseollgi/bytetrack_x_mot20.tar exactly.

MANDATORY GATE before any yoloxx20 train number is reported: re-infer val_half with the same code and settings (test_size 896x1600, nmsthre 0.7, test_conf 0.001) and reproduce the supplied datasets/val_half/*/det_yoloxx20/det_yoloxx20.txt bundle. If our inference does not match the supplied detections on the half we already have, the full-train yoloxx20 row is not trustworthy and must not be published.
notes:
DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: export_embeddings.py COULD SILENTLY MISLABEL THE ReID MODEL.

In tracking/scripts/export_embeddings.py, --reid only names the artifact
directory. The model is chosen by a SEPARATE flag, --test-dataset (absent =
generic OSNet, present = FastReID SBS). Nothing tied the two together, so
  --reid fastreid-sbs-s50-mot20        (no --test-dataset)
wrote 512-dim OSNet vectors into the fastreid-sbs-s50-mot20 directory.

That is exactly what happened to the first train-split batch: all six embedding
jobs ran OSNet, three of them labelled FastReID. Detected because the OSNet and
FastReID TrackEval rows came out BYTE-IDENTICAL for all three detectors
(HOTA 80.588 / 76.311 / 75.968 twice each), which cannot happen with different
appearance models - the val_half rows differ by ~0.13 HOTA.

Root cause confirmed from the manifests, which recorded the truth even though
the directory name lied:
  .../rfdetr2xl-i4-e8-t010-nms070__fastreid-sbs-s50-mot20/train
      dimension = 512   test_dataset = False      <- actually OSNet
  .../yoloxx20__fastreid-sbs-s50-mot20/val_half
      dimension = 2048  test_dataset = True       <- genuine FastReID
Embedding files were bit-identical to their OSNet siblings (sha256 match).

FIX: new _require_slug_matches_model(reid, test_dataset) in export_embeddings.py
refuses to run when the slug's model prefix and the selected model disagree.
Verified all four combinations:
  fastreid + no --test-dataset -> REFUSED
  fastreid + --test-dataset    -> allowed
  osnet    + no --test-dataset -> allowed
  osnet    + --test-dataset    -> REFUSED
Unknown prefixes are unconstrained, so this adds no policy where none existed.

REMEDIATION: the three mislabelled embedding sets and the tracks and metrics
derived from them were moved to
artifacts/tmp/mislabelled-fastreid-actually-osnet-2026-09-09/ (moved, not
deleted) and re-run with --test-dataset. New MOT20-01 FastReID files are
191-229 MB against OSNet's ~40 MB, the expected 2048 vs 512 dimension ratio.
The three OSNet runs were correct throughout and are unaffected.

NOT A REGRESSION IN PUBLISHED NUMBERS: every val_half row in
docs/results-reference.md section 7.2 has test_dataset = True in its manifest,
so no existing result is affected. The trap was latent and this was the first
run to hit it.
close_reason:
Complete 2026-09-09. Results in docs/mot20-train-evaluation.md (added to
.claude/project/docs-index.md). All three detectors evaluated over the entire
MOT20 train split, 8,931 frames, 1,134,614 GT boxes, 2,215 GT identities, both
ReID models each.

DETECTION mAP@50:95 - arm E 0.7653, I4 0.7184, yoloxx20-official 0.7156.
TRACKEVAL HOTA - arm E/osnet 80.588, arm E/fastreid 80.541, I4/fastreid 76.353,
yolox-official/osnet 76.311, I4/osnet 75.968, yolox-official/fastreid 75.931.

Arm E's +4.2 HOTA lead is an artifact of its design, not model quality: its own
curve reaches EMA 0.7033 at epoch 7 (where I4 stops) and 0.7588 at epoch 19, so
the whole margin is generated after I4's stopping point, on frames inside its
training set. I4 and the official YOLOX are tied at 76.353 vs 76.311, a 0.042
gap. Every figure is training-set fit; no row may join a val_half table.

FOUR LATENT DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, each recorded in the notes above:
 1. The supplied yoloxx20 bundle is NOT ByteTrack's official release, and the
    official checkpoint is stronger (val_half mAP@50:95 0.7135 vs 0.6759). Every
    published RF-DETR-vs-baseline margin was measured against a weaker model.
 2. BoostTrack's ECC warp cache was keyed by sequence name only; a train run
    would have applied val_half warps and then corrupted the val_half cache.
 3. video_name doubles as the max_age lookup key with a bare-except fallback to
    30, so the fix for (2) silently halved max_age from 50 until guarded.

title: Evaluate I4 on val_half as a matched-contamination parity check against yoloxx20
description:
The yoloxx20 baseline trained on val_half, so every arm A-D comparison against
it carries the section 0 caveat. I4 also trained on val_half. Measuring I4 on
val_half therefore gives the FIRST like-for-like comparison the project can
make: both detectors asked about frames they trained on, which is the condition
ByteTrack reports its own MOT20 numbers under.

Chain: export detections from last_ema.pth -> derive t010-nms070 -> OSNet
embeddings -> BoostTrack++ defaults -> TrackEval, plus analyze_detections.py
under the standard matrix protocol.

parity check, not a quality measurement, and its numbers must be kept in a
separate table from the held-out results.

unavailable and the usual checksum could not be used. Substituted a directional
gate: I4 trained on these frames, so its mAP must land well ABOVE arms A-D's
held-out ~0.62 or something is wrong. It returned 0.7068 against arm D's 0.6282
on the same internal measurement, +0.0786, which confirms both the geometry

  AssA        73.110       67.133     +5.977
  DetRe       83.137       76.687     +6.450
  DetPr       86.204       87.688     -1.484
  LocA        87.480       88.177     -0.697

  IDSW         1,145        1,013       +132

DETECTION, same protocol as the matrix:

  mAP@75        0.8808     0.8278
  mAP@50:95     0.7178     0.6759

title: Arm E: contaminated-validation diagnostic to fork the I7 decay question
description:
Running since 2026-09-08 14:31 in tmux session mot20, window arme-diagnostic.
Run dir finetuning/artifacts/rfdetr-2xl-arme-diagnostic-2026-09-08-r1.
Config finetuning/configs/rfdetr_2xl_i5-arm-e-contaminated-val-diagnostic.toml.
Launcher finetuning/scripts/run_rfdetr_2xl_arm_e_diagnostic.sh.

I4's recipe exactly, except the valid split is MOT20 val_half - which is also in
its training set, 4,463/4,463 verified overlap. Deliberate.

PURPOSE. I7 is unexplained: every held-out arm peaks in single-digit epochs then
declines without recovering. Arms A-D only ever measured the held-out side of
that curve, which cannot separate the two live causes. This measures the
training-set side, which forks the question:

  training-set MOT20 fit RISES while held-out falls
      -> classic overfitting; fix is regularization / early stopping
  training-set MOT20 fit ALSO FALLS
      -> refutes overfitting outright, since nothing overfits while getting
         worse on its own training data. Points at mixture interference (68.4%
         CrowdHuman pulling capacity away from MOT20), the LR schedule, or EMA.

Deltas from I4: valid split val_half rather than empty; epochs 8 -> 20;
checkpoint_interval 4 -> 1. Seven GPUs retained deliberately so effective batch
stays 56 and arm E's epoch N is comparable to I4's epoch N; arm E's first 8
epochs should approximately reproduce I4, which is a free consistency check.

Every epoch is checkpointed because there is no valid "best" on a contaminated
split. Each .ckpt carries both weight branches (state_dict and
callbacks.RFDETREMACallback.average_model_state_dict), so either is recoverable
per epoch for later HOTA work. ~2.0 GB/epoch, ~40 GB for 20.

Stopped by the operator once 6 consecutive epochs fail to beat the running best
EMA mAP@50:95. No automatic early stopping.

THIS IS A DIAGNOSTIC, NOT A CANDIDATE MODEL. Every val/* number it produces is a
training-set fit measurement. It must never share a table with arms A-D. The
dataset audit refused to start it until `contaminated_validation` was declared
in the config, and records the overlap in run-provenance.json.

Evidence when complete: finetuning/experiments.md.
close_reason:
Complete 2026-09-08, 20 epochs. The diagnostic answers its question decisively: OVERFITTING IS CONFIRMED, NOT REFUTED.

The stated refutation condition was that if training-set MOT20 fit also declines, overfitting is ruled out and the cause is mixture interference, the LR schedule, or EMA. It does not decline. It improves for the entire run and the BEST EPOCH IS THE LAST ONE.

| epoch | mAP@50:95 | EMA | val_loss | val_loss_bbox | recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.6106 | 0.6025 | 6.2108 | 0.0171 | 0.9176 |
| 5 | 0.6878 | 0.6909 | 5.1237 | 0.0130 | 0.9429 |
| 10 | 0.7150 | 0.7208 | 4.8033 | 0.0116 | 0.9505 |
| 15 | 0.7349 | 0.7432 | 4.5332 | 0.0108 | 0.9616 |
| 19 | **0.7533** | **0.7588** | **4.3161** | **0.0100** | **0.9689** |

Every quantity moves the right way for 20 straight epochs: mAP +0.1427, val_loss -1.895, val_loss_bbox -0.0071 (a 42% reduction), recall +0.0513. The only non-monotonicity is two wobbles of 0.0005 and 0.0004 at e9 and e15, an order of magnitude below the 0.003-0.007 per-epoch noise floor measured in mot-6po.

CONTRAST THAT WITH THE HELD-OUT ARMS, same architecture and recipe family:

| arm | validation | peak epoch | behaviour after peak |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | held out | 5 of 50 | declines to e49, -0.0370 (7.2 SD) |
| B | held out | 1 of 30 | declines to e29, -0.0453 (14.2 SD) |
| C | held out | 9 of 100 | declines to e99, -0.0560 (21.5 SD) |
| D | held out | 13 of 30 | declines to e29, -0.0117 (1.7 SD, not established) |
| **E** | **contaminated** | **19 of 20** | **no turnover at all** |

Training-set fit rising monotonically while held-out fit peaks in single-digit epochs and declines is the definition of overfitting. Mixture interference, the LR schedule and EMA are not required to explain the decay, and arm E removes them as necessary causes.

This corroborates the loss decomposition recorded on mot-ayx today: across the held-out arms the decay is localization-specific (loss_bbox degrades 9.9-41.4% from peak while recall stays flat and precision improves). Arm E shows the same quantity moving the OPPOSITE way on seen data (loss_bbox 0.0171 -> 0.0100). The model is progressively fitting box regression to the training images at the expense of unseen ones.

CAVEAT ON ABSOLUTE VALUES. Arm E's 0.7533 is not comparable to any held-out figure: it validates on data it trained on. Only the SHAPE of the curve is evidence, and only against the held-out arms' shape.

SECONDARY DELIVERABLE. 20 per-epoch checkpoints are on disk in the run directory, which is what mot-n2n.1 needs to measure duplicate rate against training progress without a new training run.

title: Export arm C's detections and measure its duplicate rate
description:
The phenomenon is established; the cause is not.

Established: arm A emits 33.219 overlapping pairs per frame at IoU >= 0.75 in
4,463 of 4,463 frames. The control now exists — `tracking/scripts/analyze_gt_overlap.py`
applies the identical pairwise rule to `gt.txt`, where every box is a distinct
annotated person, and finds 0.585 pairs per frame (42.06% of frames, max GT-GT
IoU 0.983). So real crowding accounts for under 2% of the observed rate and
~32.6 pairs per frame are unexplained. NMS at IoU 0.70 removes them, worth
+0.63 HOTA.

Not established: whether MOT20's density (137.8 instances/image, ~19x COCO) or
CrowdHuman's sparsity (81% of training images averaging 22.7 persons) drives it.
Arm A and arm D are both CrowdHuman-heavy and cannot separate the two.

Do:
1. Export arm C's detections at `-t005`. Arm C trained on MOT20 only, no
   CrowdHuman, so its duplicate rate is the discriminating measurement. Same
   rate implicates density; a sharp drop implicates the training mix and makes
   this a data question rather than an architectural one.
2. Extend `analyze_detections.py` to match predictions to GT and count
   predictions-per-GT directly, across score thresholds. The GT control bounds
   the confound; matching removes it. The current figure counts raw prediction
   pairs and does not distinguish two boxes on one person from two boxes on two
   overlapping people.

Evidence: `docs/experiment-report.md` section 2.3,
`artifacts/tracking/gt-overlap-val_half.json`, `docs/results-reference.md`
sections 1.2b and 4.
close_reason:
Done 2026-09-08. Arm C exported (rfdetr2xl-armc-e9-t005, geometry checksum
expected 0.6139 observed 0.6143 MATCH) and analysed under the standard
detection-matrix protocol. The result REFUTES the hypothesis it was filed to
test, and points somewhere new.

The CrowdHuman-sparsity hypothesis is dead. Arm C trained on MOT20 only, never
saw a sparse image, and duplicates 47% WORSE than arm A:

  arm C  (100% MOT20,  4,489 train imgs)  48.984 dup/frame  297.73 boxes  max 390
  arm A  (18.8% MOT20, 23,859)            33.219            283.54       max 386
  arm D  (18.8% MOT20, 23,859)            31.400            282.74       max 383
  I4     (31.6% MOT20, 28,322)            28.923            286.37       max 386
  ground truth control                     0.585            137.80       max 220

Arm C also saturates the num_select=390 ceiling exactly and is the weakest arm
on every accuracy metric (mAP@50:95 0.6258 against arm A 0.6369, arm D 0.6446).
Duplication and accuracy move together.

A GT control was built to make these numbers readable at all:
tracking/scripts/analyze_gt_overlap.py applies the identical pairwise rule to
gt.txt, where every box is a distinct annotated person. Real person-on-person
overlap at IoU>=0.75 is 0.585/frame in 42% of frames (max GT-GT IoU 0.983), so
it is real but explains under 2% of the observed rate. Filed because external
review correctly noted the original duplicate metric never matched predictions
to ground truth.

WHAT THE ORDERING NOW SUGGESTS. Duplicates do not track MOT20 share (arm C has
the highest share and the worst rate). They track TOTAL TRAINING IMAGES,
monotonically: 4,489 -> 23,859 -> 28,322 gives 48.98 -> 33.2/31.4 -> 28.9. That
points at under-training / incomplete convergence of the one-to-one assignment
rather than density or mixture composition.

Stated as a lead, not a conclusion. Two reasons to be careful: arm C also
differs in schedule (100 epochs, peak at 9) and I4's 28.9 is confounded because
I4 trained on the frames it is measured on, so cleaner predictions are expected
for free. The arm C vs arm A/D comparison is the clean part and it alone spans
4,489 vs 23,859 images.

Follow-up filed separately for the remaining confound and for a GT-matched

title: Phase 8b: root-cause the HOTA deficit
description:
Determine whether the deficit came from tracker integration, ReID, association
settings, annotation conventions, or the detector itself, before spending any
GPU time on a retrain.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Root-cause analysis",
`docs/results-reference.md` sections 1.2, 4, 5, 6.
close_reason:
Done, and it changed the framing of the whole project.

Ruled out: annotation conventions (val_half COCO labels are byte-identical to
gt.txt at mean IoU 0.9995); tracker-side degradation (mean matched IoU is
0.8334 before the tracker and 0.8343 after, so no post-detection stage harms
box quality); and detector superiority itself (under one pycocotools protocol
the baseline has the higher mAP@50:95, 0.6759 against 0.6297).

tracking" was wrong; RF-DETR led only at IoU 0.5.

title: Fix embedding cache keying so variant swaps cannot reuse stale vectors
description:

(`./cache/embeddings/{video}_embedding.pkl`, loaded via `tag.split(":")[0]`).
Its only guard compares cached embedding count against detection count.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Cache-keying hazard".
close_reason:
Done. The upstream guard cannot detect a changed ReID model over unchanged
detections: the counts match and stale vectors from the previous model are
returned silently, which would have corrupted every comparison in this project
without ever raising an error.

title: Share one long-side cap between training and detection export
description:

Evidence: `finetuning/src/mot20/detection/rfdetr_training.py`,

title: I8: compare CrowdHuman's box convention against MOT20's
description:
Phase 8b proved the *validation* labels are byte-identical to gt.txt at mean
IoU 0.9995. It never checked the *training* labels, and CrowdHuman is 81% of
them. CrowdHuman full-body boxes are amodal annotator estimates of occluded
extent, produced by a different process than MOT20's.

If the conventions differ systematically, that is a second mechanism for the
localization jitter and it changes what a mix experiment should look like.

Compare on a normalised basis: aspect ratio, visible-to-full ratio, and how
each treats truncation at the image border. No GPU required, and it targets the
largest remaining gap (LocA 2.856).

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I8,
`docs/experiment-report.md` section 3.
notes:
STATE 2026-09-08. New steer from the I4 parity run, worth reading before
starting this.

I4 trained on val_half and its LocA rose to 87.480 from arm D's 85.321, +2.159,
purely from having memorised those boxes. Held out, arm D sits 2.856 below the
yoloxx20 baseline; contaminated, that gap nearly closes.

That is diagnostic: the model CAN place boxes precisely when it has seen them.
So the localization deficit is substantially a GENERALIZATION failure, not a
fixed convention offset or a geometry error. A systematic
CrowdHuman-vs-MOT20 box-convention mismatch would not disappear just because the
frames were memorised.

This does not close the issue - a convention difference could still contribute,
and measuring it is cheap and CPU-only. But it lowers the prior that a
convention offset is the main cause, and it raises the priority of mot-gpf
(regression loss weighting) and of anything that improves generalization.
close_reason:
I8 measured 2026-09-08, CPU only. Answer in one line: the convention difference is REAL but it does NOT transfer, so it is not the localization mechanism.

MEASUREMENT 1 — the conventions do differ. Arm D's training manifest (datasets/finetuning/rfdetr-mot20-crowdhuman-byte65-test-adapted-2026-09-04), interior boxes only so border clipping cannot confound, median aspect ratio w/h stratified by relative box height:

| band h/imgH | MOT20 n | MOT20 | CrowdHuman n | CH | CH/MOT20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05-0.10 | 43,915 | 0.463 | 104,996 | 0.425 | 0.917 |
| 0.10-0.15 | 310,014 | 0.425 | 67,789 | 0.395 | 0.930 |
| 0.15-0.25 | 142,371 | 0.413 | 81,182 | 0.380 | 0.920 |
| 0.25-0.50 | 4,540 | 0.394 | 94,423 | 0.360 | 0.914 |

CrowdHuman boxes are 8-9% narrower per unit height, and the ratio is stable across every comparable band, so it is a convention offset and not a size artifact. The 0.00-0.05 band is not usable (MOT20 n=167). CrowdHuman also carries no visibility field, so the visible-to-full comparison the issue asked for cannot be made from this manifest; MOT20's visibility has median 0.543 with only 13.2% fully visible. Border treatment differs by framing, not by convention: no box in EITHER source extends past the image bounds (outside fraction 0.0000 both), so CrowdHuman's amodal boxes were clipped at conversion. Edge-touching rates differ as camera geometry predicts (CrowdHuman bottom 0.100 vs MOT20 0.045; MOT20 top 0.073 vs CrowdHuman 0.011). iscrowd is 22.5% in CrowdHuman against 11.2% in MOT20.

MEASUREMENT 2 — the model did not inherit it. Arm D detections vs val_half ground truth, IoU>=0.5 matched pairs, 116,390 pairs, score>=0.5, every 5th frame:

| Sequence | matched | pred w/h | gt w/h | ratio | w ratio | h ratio | mean IoU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOT20-01 | 1,993 | 0.405 | 0.409 | 0.990 | 0.992 | 0.996 | 0.8453 |
| MOT20-02 | 17,431 | 0.401 | 0.398 | 1.005 | 1.016 | 1.005 | 0.8300 |
| MOT20-03 | 36,452 | 0.433 | 0.446 | 0.970 | 0.984 | 1.002 | 0.8168 |
| MOT20-05 | 60,514 | 0.431 | 0.429 | 1.003 | 1.016 | 1.009 | 0.8383 |
| ALL | 116,390 | 0.427 | 0.429 | 0.994 | 1.008 | 1.006 | 0.8304 |

Predicted shape matches MOT20 convention to within 0.6%, with width and height ratios both within 1%. If the 8-9% CrowdHuman narrowing had propagated, the ratio would sit near 0.92. It does not.

CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE AS WRITTEN. The description says CrowdHuman is '81% of' the training labels. That is the IMAGE share (19,370 of 23,859). By BOX count, which is what the regression loss actually sees, it is 566,493 CrowdHuman against 584,950 MOT20 — MOT20 is the slight majority at 51%. That is very likely why the convention does not transfer, and it means the premise that made this a high-prior hypothesis was off.

CONCLUSION. Mean matched-pair IoU is 0.8304 with essentially zero shape bias, so the entire localization deficit is SCATTER, not offset. Nothing here is correctable by re-annotating or re-weighting a convention. This confirms by direct measurement what the 2026-09-08 note inferred from I4's contaminated LocA rise (85.321 -> 87.480): the deficit is a generalization failure. It raises the priority of mot-gpf (regression loss weighting) and lowers the priority of any convention-alignment work, which should now be considered closed rather than pending.

title: I7a: fix the training schedule that makes every arm decay
description:
All four arms peak in single-digit epochs and then decline monotonically for
the remainder of the run. Arm A lost 0.037 mAP over its last 45 epochs. This is
compute being spent to make the model worse, reproduced on every mix and at two
different input resolutions, and no hypothesis has been tested.

`lr_scheduler = "step"` with `lr_drop` at 24 or 40 never fires usefully because
the peak arrives long before the drop. A short cosine run is the obvious
candidate and is the cheapest training experiment available, because it is
short by construction.

Evidence: `docs/results-reference.md` sections 3.1-3.4,
`docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I7.
notes:
STATE 2026-09-08. Still open and still unexplained. Two candidate fixes were
examined today; one is largely eliminated, and a diagnostic is now running.

ELIMINATED (mostly): the augmentation ramp-down. ByteTrack's MOT20 recipe sets
no_aug_epochs = 10, disabling mosaic/mixup for the last 10 of 80 epochs, which
is a deliberate trick to make the FINAL checkpoint reliably the best - it is why
"take the last checkpoint" is safe for them and risky for us. Checked whether
RF-DETR has an equivalent: it does not. grep finds no no_aug/close_mosaic knob
in the installed package, and per Roboflow's docs the augmentation stack is a
static whole-run setting with NO mosaic or MixUp at all. Our augmentation is
already light (multi_scale + horizontal flip), so a ramp-down has little to bite
on. Not worth a training run ahead of better candidates. Could still be tested
cheaply by disabling multi_scale for the last epochs via a resume.

RULED OUT PREVIOUSLY: training mix (arm C decays without CrowdHuman) and
resolution (arm D decays at max_size 1600).

NEW CORRELATION, untested as cause: arm C is simultaneously the fastest-decaying
arm, the worst duplicator (48.984/frame), the one that saturates the num_select
ceiling, and the one with least training data (4,489 images). Duplicate rate
across all arms tracks total training images monotonically. That is consistent
with the decay and the duplication being one under-convergence phenomenon rather
than two. See mot-n2n.1.

ACTIVE DIAGNOSTIC: mot-yk3.1 (arm E) is running and is the discriminating
experiment. Arms A-D only ever measured the held-out side of the decay curve.
Arm E measures the training-set side. If training-set MOT20 fit also declines,
overfitting is refuted outright and the cause is mixture interference, the LR
schedule, or EMA. Do not start an I7a fix run until arm E reports - it changes
which fix is worth trying.

Arm E also checkpoints every epoch, so the per-epoch duplicate rate can be
measured from its checkpoints without a new run.
2026-09-08 from mot-6po (I7b), relevant to root-causing the decay: the per-epoch noise floor of val/mAP_50_95 is now measured. Epoch-to-epoch SD of the regular branch is 0.0051 (arm A), 0.0032 (B), 0.0026 (C), 0.0070 (D). Any decay analysis must clear that floor before calling a decline real. Arm A's regular branch peaked at epoch 5 of 50 and never recovered, which is the cleanest instance of the pattern on disk. Also note checkpoint selection is a max over ~2xN noisy evaluations (100 draws in arm A), so reported 'best' values are upward-biased and arm-to-arm gaps below ~0.005 should not be read as real.
ANALYSIS 2026-09-08, CPU only, from the stored metrics.csv files. The issue says 'no hypothesis has been tested'. That is no longer true: the validation loss curves identify the decay's mechanism, and it is narrower than 'the model gets worse'.

THE DECAY IS LOCALIZATION, NOT DETECTION. From each arm's own peak to its final epoch:

| arm | recall | precision | mAP@50 | mAP@50:95 | loss_ce | loss_bbox | loss_giou |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (e5 -> e49) | -1.1% | +1.9% | -1.5% | -6.0% | +7.6% | +26.9% | +17.0% |
| B (e1 -> e29) | -1.0% | +2.4% | -2.5% | -7.4% | +14.0% | +41.4% | +24.0% |
| C (e9 -> e99) | -1.8% | +1.8% | -3.0% | -9.1% | +14.4% | +38.1% | +24.1% |
| D (e13 -> e29) | -0.4% | +0.6% | -1.0% | -1.9% | +2.2% | +9.9% | +6.7% |

Recall is essentially flat and precision actually IMPROVES in every arm. The model does not stop finding people. mAP@50 barely moves while mAP@50:95 falls three to five times faster, which is the signature of boxes that are still on the right objects but placed progressively worse. loss_bbox is the worst-degrading term in all four arms without exception, giou second, classification a distant third.

This is a textbook overfitting curve, visible directly: train/loss falls monotonically throughout (arm A 9.53 -> 3.99, arm B 5.77 -> 2.93) while val/loss turns around at exactly the epoch mAP peaks (arm A minimum 6.0166 at e5, rising to 6.6603 by e49). The val-loss minimum coincides with the mAP peak in every arm.

THE DECAY IS REAL, not noise. Against the per-arm noise floor measured in mot-6po: arm A 7.2 SD, arm B 14.2 SD, arm C 21.5 SD. Arm D is the exception at 1.7 SD, i.e. arm D's decline is NOT established — it is within what its own epoch-to-epoch volatility could produce.

DECAY RATE TRACKS DATASET DIVERSITY. Normalised per 1,000 optimisation steps, which is this project's convention for comparing arms:

| arm | peak step | end step | drop | drop per 1k steps | unique images |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 2,237 | 18,649 | -0.0370 | -0.0023 | 23,859 |
| B | 1,165 | 17,489 | -0.0453 | -0.0028 | 4,468 MOT20 x4 + CrowdHuman |
| C | 709 | 7,099 | -0.0560 | **-0.0088** | 4,489 |
| D | 5,221 | 11,189 | -0.0117 | -0.0020 | 23,859 |

Arm C decays three to four times faster per step than any other arm. It is the only arm with no CrowdHuman, so it has roughly a fifth of the unique imagery and revisits it that much more often. Arm B, which oversamples MOT20 4x but retains CrowdHuman, decays at a third of arm C's rate. Read together, CrowdHuman's 19,370 unique images are acting as a regulariser, and the decay rate is closer to a function of unique-image diversity than of mixture ratio.

CONSEQUENCES:
1. The fix candidates should be reweighted. A cosine schedule addresses when learning stops, but the failing quantity is specifically box regression on held-out data. That makes mot-gpf (regression loss weighting) a more targeted candidate than a schedule change, and it agrees with mot-8r3, which showed the localization deficit is scatter with zero shape bias.
2. Early stopping is nearly free and currently unused. Every arm peaks in single-digit epochs and never recovers, so the compute after the peak is not merely wasted, it is harmful.
3. Arm D's recipe already suppresses most of the effect. Its decay is 1.7 SD and -0.0020 per 1k steps, the mildest measured. Whatever arm D changed relative to arm A is worth isolating before a new schedule is designed.
4. This strengthens mot-n2n.1: volume and density are separable through the per-step decay rate above, without waiting for new runs.

ARM E, still running, is consistent with overfitting so far rather than against it. At epoch 6 it reports val/mAP_50_95 0.6973 on its contaminated (training-set) validation, still at its own maximum with no turnover. The stated refutation condition was that training-set fit must DECLINE; it is rising. Not yet decisive, since the held-out arms did not turn over until e5-e13 either, so arm E needs to run past that window before it settles anything.

No fix run started, per the standing instruction on this issue to wait for arm E.
ARM E REPORTED, 2026-09-08. The standing instruction on this issue was to wait for it before starting a fix run. It is done, and it settles the mechanism: OVERFITTING CONFIRMED.

Arm E ran 20 epochs on contaminated (training-set) validation and its BEST EPOCH IS THE LAST: mAP 0.6106 -> 0.7533, EMA -> 0.7588, val_loss 6.2108 -> 4.3161, val_loss_bbox 0.0171 -> 0.0100, recall 0.9176 -> 0.9689. No turnover anywhere. The only non-monotonicity is two wobbles of 0.0005 and 0.0004, an order of magnitude under the noise floor.

The refutation condition stated here — training-set fit must decline — is not met. It rises for the whole run while the held-out arms peak at e1, e5, e9 and e13 and then decline. Mixture interference, the LR schedule and EMA are removed as NECESSARY causes.

Note the direction of the bbox term, which ties this to the loss decomposition above. On held-out data val_loss_bbox degrades 9.9-41.4% after the peak. On seen data it improves 42%. The same quantity moves opposite ways depending only on whether the model has seen the image. The model is progressively fitting box regression to the training images at the cost of unseen ones.

WHAT THIS MAKES THE FIX. The question is no longer 'why does it decay' but 'how do we regularise box regression, or stop before it hurts'. In rough order of cost:

1. EARLY STOPPING / a schedule that ends near the peak. Nearly free, currently unused, and every arm peaks in single digits. Not a fix for the underlying weakness but it recovers the lost mAP immediately.
2. mot-gpf, regression loss weighting. Now the best-motivated training change: the failing term is specifically bbox, and mot-8r3 showed the residual localization error is scatter with zero systematic shape bias.
3. More unique imagery or stronger augmentation. Supported by the decay-rate-versus-diversity result above (arm C, the only arm without CrowdHuman, decays 3-4x faster per step than any other). CrowdHuman is already acting as a regulariser; our augmentation is light, and mot-5zl showed multi_scale is largely inert for the wide sequences, so there is real headroom.

A cosine schedule remains reasonable but is no longer the leading candidate: it changes when learning stops, not what is being overfitted.

Still no fix run started. This issue calls for a retrain, which the current scope defers.

title: I6: test whether raising the training long-side cap closes the gap
description:
Arm D against arm A with byte-identical manifests, changing only geometry.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I6,
`docs/experiment-report.md`.
close_reason:
Done. I6 WORKS, BUT NOT BY ITS STATED MECHANISM.

Arm D reaches HOTA 70.777 against the baseline's 70.208 and arm A's 68.809 —
the first configuration in this project to beat the baseline, +0.569 and +1.968
respectively. Also ahead on MOTA (+2.945), IDF1 (+3.101), Frag (-1,539) and MT
(+150).

The mechanism contradicts the rationale. I6 was proposed to fix box regression.
LocA moved 85.190 -> 85.321, by 0.131, and remains 2.856 below the baseline,
even though mAP@75 on the exported checkpoint improved 0.7400 -> 0.7523. That
mAP gain did not survive contact with the tracker's operating point.

The gain is association: AssA +2.810 over arm A, now exceeding the baseline's
by 1.642. The route is recall, DetRe 76.952 -> 78.256 and 8,082 fewer false
negatives, giving the tracker more continuous evidence per identity.

So the localization deficit is real, unfixed, and still the largest single gap
to the baseline. It is simply no longer the binding constraint on HOTA.
Precision remains the other weakness: DetPr 82.300 against 87.688, 21,242 false
positives against 6,947.

title: I5: test whether the CrowdHuman/MOT20 mix causes the early peak
description:
Three single-variable arms sweeping the MOT20 share across essentially its
whole range, on the ablation build so val_half stays a valid yardstick.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I5,
`docs/results-reference.md` sections 3.1-3.3.
close_reason:
Done. HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED.

MOT20 share 18.8% -> 48.0% -> 100% gives peak mAP@50:95 0.6202 / 0.6168 /
0.6139. That is a spread of 0.0063, about 1% relative, and it moves the WRONG
way: the unmodified arm A is the best of the three. All three arms reproduce
the same early-peak-then-monotone-decline shape, so removing CrowdHuman
entirely does not fix it.

Two consequences. The measured reasoning about scale and density regimes, while
correct as measurement, does not predict the outcome, and is retained as a
recorded hypothesis that testing rejected. And the post-peak decline is not the
training mix, which raised the prior on I6 and led directly to arm D.

One claim from this issue was later corrected: the duplicate-prediction rate
cannot be attributed to arm C, because arm C's detections were never exported.
See e5-armc-duplicates.

title: Audit the RF-DETR data transform, target retention, and collator padding
description:
Establish what geometry the model actually sees, because the configured
`resolution` is not necessarily what binds.

Evidence:
`finetuning/docs/experiments/2026-09-04-rfdetr-loader-geometry-audit.md`,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 4.3.
close_reason:
Done, and it produced the single most consequential finding in the detector
workstream. The training transform is `RandomResize([1120],
max_size=_COCO_MAX_SIZE)` with `_COCO_MAX_SIZE = 1333`. At MOT20's 1920x1080
the 1333 cap binds, not the 1120 target: the model sees 1333x750, a scale of
0.694, and the `resolution = 1120` setting is inert.

The baseline YOLOX-X runs `test_size = (896, 1600)` -> 1593x896, scale 0.830,
and therefore sees every pedestrian about 20% larger. That gap became I6, and
arm D closed it by setting `max_size = 1600` for an effective 0.833.

title: Score every detection variant under one pycocotools protocol
description:
Neither detector's own evaluation code can be trusted for a cross-detector
comparison. Score both through identical pycocotools against the same
annotations.

Evidence: `tracking/scripts/analyze_detections.py`,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 4.1.
close_reason:
Done for six variants including arm D, completed 2026-09-08. Same `valid`
annotations, MOT20 ignore regions carried as `iscrowd`, `maxDets = 390` for
every variant.

Required reading the COCOeval accumulator directly: pycocotools' `summarize()`
computes the headline AP with a hardcoded `maxDets = 100` that is absent from
this list and silently yields -1.

Result: the baseline wins mAP@50:95 for both arms — 0.6759 against arm A's
0.6297 and arm D's 0.6351 — while RF-DETR wins mAP@50, up to 0.9663 against
0.9000. A crossover at IoU threshold, which is the signature of a localization
deficit rather than a recall deficit. Arm D improves every mAP column over arm
A, with the largest gain at mAP@75 (+0.0120), and still does not change the
verdict.

title: Build the layered L0-L4 artifact store with manifests
description:
A tracking result is a composition of detector, ReID model, and tracker
settings. Storing only end results makes the grid unreproducible and forces
recomputation whenever one factor changes.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Artifact Levels and Variant Naming".
close_reason:
Done, under `artifacts/tracking/`: L0 ECC, L1 detections per detector variant,
L2 embeddings per detector+ReID pair, L3 tracks per full combination, L4
metrics. Every level writes a manifest, so any cell of the grid is reproducible
from its path plus its manifests.

Two design decisions that carried weight. L2 embeddings are computed for every
exported detection rather than only those surviving a tracker's `det_thresh`,
which makes them independent of tracker configuration and is what makes the
grid composable at all. And the published YOLOX detections already present
under `datasets/val_half/<sequence>/det_yoloxx20/` are registered as an
ordinary detector variant rather than a special case, so the baseline is one
cell of the same grid and runs through identical code.

title: I1: sweep suppression IoU and adopt greedy NMS at 0.70
description:
RF-DETR exports without NMS by design. Test whether that is right for MOT20.

Evidence: `docs/tracker-improvements.md` section I1,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 7.1.
close_reason:
Done. Suppression IoU none / 0.70 / 0.60 / 0.50 gives HOTA 68.175 / 68.809 /
68.510 / 66.076. Adopted 0.70, which matches the `nmsthre` the published YOLOX
detections were produced with, worth +0.63 HOTA.

The finding that mattered beyond the setting itself: NMS *lowers* mAP@50:95
(0.6337 -> 0.6297) while *raising* HOTA. COCO AP tolerates extra low-ranked
duplicates that a tracker must resolve into identities. Optimising the detector
on AP alone would have kept the worse setting, which is the first hard evidence
that mAP is not a sufficient selection signal for this project.

title: Measure localization before and after the tracker
description:
Separate how much IoU is lost from why, and determine whether any
post-detection stage degrades box quality.

Evidence: `tracking/scripts/analyze_localization.py`,
`docs/results-reference.md` section 5, `docs/experiment-report.md` section 3.
close_reason:
Done for nine variants including arm D, completed 2026-09-08. Hungarian match
against gt.txt at IoU 0.5, detections filtered at score >= 0.40, per-edge
residuals normalised by ground-truth box size.

Three findings. The error is jitter, not an offset: signed residual means are
near zero on every edge for every variant while absolute means are 1.22-1.44x
the baseline's, so there is no systematic shift to subtract out. The tracker is
not the culprit: mean matched IoU is 0.8356 for arm D's detections and 0.8362
for its tracks, 0.8713 and 0.8726 for the baseline. And resolution barely
touched it: arm D's absolute residuals are 0.0603/0.0611/0.0225/0.0445 against
arm A's 0.0602/0.0629/0.0234/0.0449, with mean matched IoU moving 0.8336 ->
0.8356.

description:
The first end-to-end comparison, holding tracker and ReID fixed and varying
only the detector.

Evidence: `docs/results-reference.md` section 7,
`docs/tracker-experiments.md` "Stage 1".

title: Prove the training labels and gt.txt are the same boxes
description:
The detector is scored against COCO annotations; HOTA is scored against
`gt.txt`. If those two label sets disagreed, every comparison between mAP and
HOTA would be measuring an annotation artifact rather than the detector.

Evidence: `docs/results-reference.md` section 1.2,
`artifacts/tracking/annotation-agreement-val_half.json`.
close_reason:
Done, and the answer is unambiguous. Measured directly against each other with
no model involved: 615,137 matched pairs, GT coverage 1.0000, COCO coverage
1.0000, mean matched IoU 0.9995, median 1.0000, fraction at IoU >= 0.95 of
0.9998. Mean edge residuals are 0.0000 on x1/x2/y1 and -0.0005 on y2.

The two label sets are the same boxes. A label-convention mismatch is therefore
excluded as an explanation for any mAP-versus-HOTA disagreement, which is what
made the later root-cause work tractable.

Evidence: `repos/BoostTrack/main.py`; the contract this violates is in
`docs/tracker-experiments.md` (artifact/variant naming). Originally recorded in
`docs/tracker-todo.md` Phase 9, which was deleted when tracking moved to Beads.

One-class pedestrian detector for MOT20, from base checkpoint through the

title: Integrate and validate the revised Focus review workflow
description:
## Why
The event controls, timeline, trajectory, and loading behavior must work together across synthetic edge cases and real read-only MOT20 review before the epic can be accepted.

## What
Exercise each event family, every pair, and all three; cover thresholds, races, gaps, no-event states, past/full trajectory, timeline seeking, delayed loading, new-control axe scans, console/network state, desktop/narrow screenshots, source-integrity manifests, pointer-latency and browser-performance comparison, operator documentation, and final user visual acceptance. Keep real MOT20 track/frame results observational and deterministic gates synthetic.
design: Implement Task 5 of the attached plan only after Tasks 1-4. Use synthetic gapped/sparse/dense fixtures for correctness and MOT20-01 track 72 only as read-only usability evidence. Update README/HANDOFF and performance evidence when measurements change.
acceptance_criteria: Focused and aggregate viewer gates pass; real and synthetic browser journeys pass without console/network/layout failures; new controls have zero serious/critical axe violations; pointer latency remains within the accepted budget; configured source manifests are unchanged; screenshots document stable geometry; and user acceptance is recorded before closing the epic.
notes:
Implementation and automated verification complete on 2026-09-03. make acceptance passed; make e2e-real passed 7 with 1 intentional narrow performance skip; source manifests are byte-identical across 2,249 configured files; all pointer p95 runs were 16.8 ms under the 50 ms budget; desktop and narrow screenshots are in track-viz/artifacts/verification/focus-review/. Task remains open solely for required user visual acceptance.
Out of scope 2026-09-08: user restricted this workstream to RF-DETR detector work only. All track-viz/viewer work is set aside, not abandoned. 4 of 5 children of mot-06v were already closed; only mot-06v.5 (integration and validation) remains.

title: Eliminate Focus playback and loading layout shifts
description:
## Why
Transient playback and review-loading messages can enter normal flow, causing the timeline, filmstrip, and lower panels to jump vertically while the reviewer watches a track. Event-refresh mount invariance is handled earlier by mot-06v.1; this issue owns playback image, observation, per-frame Context, and cross-panel geometry.

## Steps to Reproduce
Enter Focus or Context review, start playback, and observe the lower review panels while image decoding, frame observations, or per-frame Context evidence are delayed or fail. Loading states appear and disappear, moving the lower UI.

## What
Add delayed-success and delayed-failure characterization for playback-owned states, move transient statuses into overlays or fixed reserved slots, retain accessible announcements, keep one integration assertion for the Task 1 event-refresh slot, and assert stable Focus, viewport, timeline, filmstrip, and lower-panel geometry at desktop and narrow widths.
design: Implement Task 4 of the attached plan after final history controls exist. Loading feedback must not intercept controls or add normal-flow height. Task 1 owns event-refresh mount/status behavior; this issue owns image decode, observations, Context playback, and cross-panel bounding boxes.
acceptance_criteria: During Focus/Context playback with injected delays or failures, timeline and filmstrip positions vary by at most one CSS pixel; lower controls do not jump; status remains accessible; and controls stay operable unless their own action is genuinely unavailable.
close_reason: Verified overlay-based loading/error states with no normal-flow shift: 67/67 frontend tests, TypeScript, 14/14 focused desktop+narrow geometry cases, and full deterministic E2E 40 passed with 10 expected local-data skips. Image, observation, Context, and event refresh success/failure states kept Focus, viewport, timeline, filmstrip, and source-status within 1 CSS px and controls remained operable.

title: Build temporal and spatial track-history visualization
description:
## Why
The current timeline shows only endpoint, gap-start, and enabled-event markers, so continuous tracks appear as two dots and the reviewer cannot see intermediate occupancy or current progress. The short existing trace also does not offer an explicit complete-track view.

## What
Build a sequence-wide interactive history rail with occupied runs, explicit gaps, current playhead, collision-safe activity markers, pointer/keyboard seeking, and a complementary gap-aware trajectory that defaults to past-through-current and can explicitly show the complete track with future evidence distinguished.
design: Implement Task 3 of the attached plan. Use failing pure plan tests first. Preserve exact one-based seeking; implement one range-style rail control with Arrow=1 frame, Shift+Arrow=10, and Home/End bounds; render at most 256 deterministically aggregated evidence glyphs; never connect trajectory segments across gaps; cap trajectory vertices at 512 while preserving required evidence; keep static evidence under reduced-motion preferences.
acceptance_criteria: Continuous and gapped tracks visibly expose intermediate evidence and current position; range-style timeline seeking is exact and accessible; activity glyph density stays within budget and overlapping evidence remains usable; past mode contains no future evidence; complete mode is distinct; trajectory gaps remain disconnected on desktop and narrow layouts.
close_reason: Verified sequence-wide accessible rail and gap-aware trajectory: 67/67 frontend tests and TypeScript passed; full deterministic Playwright passed 28 with 10 expected local-data skips. Covers exact pointer/keyboard seeking, singleton and continuous runs, current playhead, bounded accessible evidence summary and 256-glyph aggregation, past/complete modes, future styling, reduced-motion retention, gap breaks, and <=512-vertex fallback preserving first/last/current.

title: Make review-event navigation activity-aware
description:
## Why
The current Previous/Next enabled-event controls merge displacement, scale, proximity, and meaningful confidence into one unexplained frame list. Dense proximity or accidental zero displacement/scale thresholds can therefore look like ordinary one-frame stepping.

## What
Characterize all three raw detectors without changing the backend API, derive deterministic frontend activity episodes, remove the combined navigator, add persistent family-specific counts and Previous/Next controls with diagnostic reasons, keep low-confidence navigation per-frame and separate, expose raw/activity counts, and use family-aware density warnings. Sentinel-only sources expose no track-event controls.
design: Implement Task 2 of the attached plan. Production events.py is inspect-only unless characterization proves a separately approved backend defect. Episodes never merge across missing observations. Displacement/scale anchor at greatest severity with earliest-frame ties; proximity groups by typed usable competitor ID and anchors at closest approach. Raw events remain auditable.
acceptance_criteria: On a deterministic synthetic fixture, displacement at 0.02 seeks the fixture-derived activity anchor rather than the next ordinary frame, with raw-next and grouped-anchor behavior asserted separately; default scale reports no target with a reason; continuous per-competitor proximity is one understandable activity; low confidence stays per-frame and separate; every unavailable action remains visibly and accessibly disabled.
close_reason: Verified frontend-derived activity episodes with unchanged backend contract: 59/59 frontend tests, 5/5 backend event characterizations, TypeScript, and 6 desktop/narrow Playwright cases passed. Covers gap isolation, deterministic severity ties, per-competitor proximity, separate low-confidence navigation, family-specific counts/actions, all disabled reasons, density warnings, and raw-next versus grouped-anchor behavior.

title: Stabilize Focus event settings and refresh lifecycle
description:
## Why
Typing decimal thresholds currently causes per-keystroke Focus reloads; a requested 0.02 can become 0, controls disappear, and unrelated track evidence is fetched again.

## Steps to Reproduce
Open a tracked source in Focus, enable abrupt displacement, select the threshold, and type 0.02 character by character. The Focus panel reloads after the first character, the applied threshold becomes 0, and Next enabled event can seek the next ordinary frame.

## What
Characterize the failure with a deterministic synthetic fixture, separate event refreshes from track/filmstrip loading, keep Focus content mounted, add validated draft threshold state with 300 ms debounce plus immediate Enter/blur commit, cancel stale requests, and retain the last successful state on refresh failure. This issue owns event-refresh mount invariance and its fixed status slot; playback image, observation, and per-frame Context geometry belongs to mot-06v.4.
design: Implement Task 1 of the attached plan. Invalid drafts issue no request and revert on blur with an accessible reason. Failed refreshes retain prior valid data/settings and use a non-layout-shifting retry state.
acceptance_criteria: Character-by-character entry of 0.02 remains 0.02; the existing combined next-event action seeks the exact frame derived by the synthetic characterization fixture rather than the next ordinary frame; all checkbox combinations persist; only event data refreshes; timeline and filmstrip remain mounted during success and failure.
close_reason: Verified stable event-only refresh lifecycle: frontend suite 54/54 passed, TypeScript passed, and delayed-event tracer passed in desktop and narrow Chromium; 0.02 draft, stale-response protection, checkbox composition, mounted Focus evidence, failure retry, and no evidence/filmstrip refetch are covered.

title: Improve Focus track history and event review
